---

The updated `susie_iw()` fits four independent initializations, then selects
the converged fit with the highest IW ELBO. The reference eigendecomposition
is computed once and shared across starts.

## 1. Load the example

Use the same data as the [initialization example](04-IW-eta-profile.html):
1,752 SNPs, $N=200{,}000$, $N_0=5{,}000$, $T=200$, three causal variants,
and $h^2=1\%$.

```{r}
library(susieRobust)
packageVersion("susieRobust")
packageVersion("susieR")
stopifnot(packageVersion("susieRobust") >= "0.0.0.9004")

example <- readRDS("data/iw-eta-profile/example.rds")
R0 <- example$R0; v <- example$v; N <- example$N
causal <- example$causal
```

## 2. Fit with the new defaults

The default starts are $\eta_0\in\{100,1000,5000,10000\}$, with at most
200 iterations per start and relative ELBO tolerance $10^{-4}$.
Both $\eta_0$ and $\lambda$ are estimated. `L = 10` is the number of fitted
components, not the number of reported credible sets.

```{r fit-iw}
elapsed <- system.time({
  fit <- susie_iw(v=v, R0=R0, N=N, L=10,
                  verbose=TRUE, track_fit=TRUE)
})["elapsed"]
```

`verbose = TRUE` prints a heading for each start, then iteration 1 and every
10th iteration. Each line contains the IW ELBO, $\eta_0$, $\lambda$,
$E(1/\omega)$, and `top`: the highest-posterior-probability SNP index in each
single-effect component. These indices can repeat; they are not credible sets.
The last iteration need not be printed.

`verbose` only controls messages. `track_fit = TRUE` retains every iteration
in `fit$diagnostics$multistart$traces`. The candidate summary is always saved:

```{r}
multi <- fit$diagnostics$multistart
history <- multi$history
knitr::kable(data.frame(
  Start=history$initial_eta0, eta0=history$final_eta0,
  ELBO=history$elbo, Iterations=history$iterations,
  Converged=history$converged, Selected=history$selected
), digits=3, row.names=FALSE)
```

Selection requires both the relative ELBO stopping criterion and final
parameter stationarity. If no start converges, the highest finite-ELBO fit
is returned with a warning and `converged = FALSE`. Exact ties use the first
start. Convergence does not establish a global optimum.

```{r trajectories, fig.width=10, fig.height=4.5}
traces <- multi$traces
colors <- c("grey45", "#E69F00", "#009E73", "#0072B2")
par(mfrow=c(1, 2), mar=c(4.2, 4.5, 2.5, 1))
for (parameter in c("eta0", "elbo")) {
  values <- unlist(lapply(traces, `[[`, parameter))
  plot(NA, xlim=c(1, max(history$iterations)), ylim=range(values),
       xlab="Iteration", ylab=if (parameter == "eta0") expression(eta[0]) else "IW ELBO",
       main=if (parameter == "eta0") "Eta0 after each update" else "ELBO trajectory")
  for (i in seq_along(traces)) {
    d <- traces[[i]]
    lines(d$iteration, d[[parameter]], col=colors[i], lty=i, lwd=2)
    points(tail(d$iteration, 1), tail(d[[parameter]], 1), col=colors[i], pch=19)
  }
  if (parameter == "eta0") {
    legend("topright", paste("Start", history$initial_eta0),
           col=colors, lty=seq_along(traces), lwd=2, bty="n", cex=0.8)
  }
}
par(mfrow=c(1, 1))
```

Curves begin after the first update; points mark stopping iterations.
Here the selected start is **`r format(multi$selected_initial_eta0, scientific=FALSE, big.mark=",")`**, with learned
$\eta_0 =$ `r round(fit$eta0, 3)` and
$\lambda =$ `r signif(fit$selected_lambda, 4)`.

## 3. Inspect the reported result

Printing the returned object gives the final parameter, convergence, and
credible-set summary:

```{r}
fit
```

After selecting the IW fit, 95% credible sets are filtered using reference LD
(minimum pairwise $|r|\geq0.5$) and deduplicated. If at most one set remains,
the default SER fallback replaces the reported posterior with a single-effect
RSS fit. The original IW posterior remains in `raw_fit` and `raw_pip`.
Fallback sets are also purity-filtered, so zero reported sets is possible.

```{r reported-pips, fig.width=10, fig.height=4}
plot_pip(fit, causal=causal, R=R0, main="Selected SuSiE-IW: reported PIPs")
```

Circles mark reported credible sets; red points mark the true causal SNPs.
This example reports **`r fit$reported_L` credible sets**;
SER fallback is **`r if (fit$postprocess$fallback_used) "used" else "not used"`**.

## 4. Runtime and a single start

```{r}
knitr::kable(data.frame(
  Step=c("Shared eigendecomposition", "Four IW fits", "Complete function call"),
  Seconds=c(multi$spectrum_elapsed_seconds,
            sum(history$elapsed_seconds), unname(elapsed))
), digits=3, row.names=FALSE)
```

The complete call also includes validation, selection, credible-set reporting,
and any fallback. Sharing the decomposition changes computation time, not the
fitted results for the same starts. On five local examples it reduced median
runtime by 17--72%; see the
[benchmark report](https://github.com/stephenslab/susieRobust/blob/e63485e6e9a7dc280cdfa49e03d72e723d4a2358/validation/iw-spectrum-cache/README.md).

Supply one number to run one initialization:

```{r, eval=FALSE}
fit_single <- susie_iw(v=v, R0=R0, N=N, L=10, eta0_init=1000)
```
